highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.156.0 strengthens platform support and runtime efficiency for modern Apple, Android, WebAssembly, Linux, image, stream, and text workloads.
highlights_body: The release raises Apple deployment targets, makes WebGPU builds more reliable, paces Android texture rendering with the display, and removes unnecessary allocations in frequently used image and HarfBuzzSharp paths.

bullets.detail: Apple native packages now target newer platform baselines, aligning supported iOS, macOS, and tvOS deployments with current toolchains.
The native WebGPU C++ support is bundled into libSkiaSharp, so browser applications no longer compile it on their final link line.

bullets.lead: Bundled HarfBuzz resolves locally on Linux
bullets.detail: Linux native builds bind bundled HarfBuzz functions locally, avoiding unintended symbol resolution against other libraries in the process.

bullets.lead: Android texture rendering follows the display clock
bullets.detail: Continuous GLTextureView rendering is paced by display callbacks, coalescing missed frames while preserving explicit render requests and lifecycle progress.
Disposing an SKFrontBufferedManagedStream now clears its managed stream reference even when it does not own the underlying stream.

bullets.lead: Image and HarfBuzzSharp work avoids allocations
bullets.detail: Managed image pixel copies, UTF-32 text input, and HarfBuzz feature formatting reduce temporary allocations without changing their results.

contributor_summaries.VirgilMing: Linux HarfBuzz symbol binding and more reliable Blazor CPU sample rendering tests
contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: WebAssembly WebGPU packaging that moves the native C++ support into libSkiaSharp
